full_judgment:
5. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter alia is that the plaintiff's suit is not maintainable the suit is barred by limitation and denying all the material allegations as stated in the plaint. The contention of the defendants is that one Animuddin was the sole owner of the suit land while Sivnarayan Muchi was his tenant and on the death of Sivnarayan, his son Duraprosad inherited the land and while possessing the same, Durgaproad transferred .94 acres of land by a registered kabala deed on 18.01.1952 vide kabala No.731 to Aizuddin who due to his poverty I failed to pay rents to the sole holder in consequence there of surrendered the land i.e. 'gave istafa' verbally in favour of the sole holder. Asimuddin, on getting back the land used to possess the land in question and subsequently on 11th Chaitra 1360 B.S. gave pattan by way of an unregistered patta to the defendant No.1 and 2. They also claimed to have purchased other lands appertaining to S.A. khatian No. 345 and accordingly record was prepared in their names. They further claimed to have possessed the land in question for about 46 years where they have their homestead. The learned Trial Court on perusing the documentary evidence of both sides and on hearing the parties decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs against which the defendant preferred appeal and the learned appellate court reversed the judgment and decree passed by the learned Trial Judge. 

 9. Mr. Md. Ekramul Haque, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that learned Subordinate Judge, being the last court of fact did not consider the legality and propriety of the documents of both the parties in as much as the decision of the learned court of appeal below is not based upon the consideration of the plaintiffs and defendant case side by side and thus arrived at an erroneous decision in considering the so-called unregistered patta and thereby occasioned failure of justice. 

 13. Learned Advocate further submits that the learned Trial Court in his judgment rightly found and held that the defendants failed to prove the unregistered patta of 1952 which is the basis of their claim and other documents in respect of title. On the, other hand the plaintiffs have been able to prove their title and possession, but the learned court of appeal below did not at all consider those findings of the trial court while reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court.
